title: 15. Numeracy & Number Systems: Multi-Digit Multiplication
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(23\times 4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the tens and ones separately: \(20\times 4=80\) and \(3\times 4=12\). Then add the partial products: \(80+12=92\). Therefore, \(23\times 4=92\).
questions.hint: Break the two-digit number into tens and ones before multiplying.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(34\times 2\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the tens and ones separately: \(30\times 2=60\) and \(4\times 2=8\). Then add the partial products: \(60+8=68\). Therefore, \(34\times 2=68\).
questions.hint: Multiply each place value by the one-digit number, then add.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number with regrouping.
questions.question: What is \(47\times 6\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the tens and ones separately: \(40\times 6=240\) and \(7\times 6=42\). Then add the partial products: \(240+42=282\). Therefore, \(47\times 6=282\).
questions.hint: Multiply each place value by \(6\), then combine the partial products.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(23\times 14\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply \(23\) by \(10\) and by \(4\) separately: \(23\times 10=230\) and \(23\times 4=92\). Then add the partial products: \(230+92=322\). Therefore, \(23\times 14=322\).
questions.hint: Split the two-digit multiplier into tens and ones, then add the partial products.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a three-digit number by a one-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(213\times 4\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply each place value by \(4\): \(200\times 4=800\), \(10\times 4=40\), and \(3\times 4=12\). Then add the partial products: \(800+40+12=852\). Therefore, \(213\times 4=852\).
questions.hint: Multiply the hundreds, tens, and ones separately, then add.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number with regrouping.
questions.question: What is \(36\times 25\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply \(36\) by \(20\) and by \(5\) separately: \(36\times 20=720\) and \(36\times 5=180\). Then add the partial products: \(720+180=900\). Therefore, \(36\times 25=900\).
questions.hint: Split \(25\) into \(20\) and \(5\), multiply each part, and add the results.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(124\times 32\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply \(124\) by \(30\) and by \(2\) separately: \(124\times 30=3{,}720\) and \(124\times 2=248\). Then add the partial products: \(3{,}720+248=3{,}968\). Therefore, \(124\times 32=3{,}968\).
questions.hint: Split \(32\) into \(30\) and \(2\), then add the two partial products.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number with regrouping.
questions.question: What is \(78\times 46\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply \(78\) by \(40\) and by \(6\) separately: \(78\times 40=3{,}120\) and \(78\times 6=468\). Then add the partial products: \(3{,}120+468=3{,}588\). Therefore, \(78\times 46=3{,}588\).
questions.hint: Split \(46\) into \(40\) and \(6\), then combine the partial products.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a word problem using two-digit multiplication.
questions.question: A school has \(24\) classes. Each class has \(35\) students. How many students are in the school?
questions.explanation: Multiply the number of classes by the number of students in each class: \(24\times 35\). Break \(35\) into \(30\) and \(5\): \(24\times 30=720\) and \(24\times 5=120\). Then add: \(720+120=840\). Therefore, there are \(840\) students.
questions.hint: Multiply the number of classes by the number of students per class.

questions.learningObjective: Multiply a three-digit number containing a zero by a two-digit number.
questions.question: What is \(405\times 23\)?
questions.explanation: Multiply \(405\) by \(20\) and by \(3\) separately: \(405\times 20=8{,}100\) and \(405\times 3=1{,}215\). Then add the partial products: \(8{,}100+1{,}215=9{,}315\). Therefore, \(405\times 23=9{,}315\).
questions.hint: Split \(23\) into \(20\) and \(3\), then add the partial products.
